cards.title: Core idea
cards.body: Choose a database from access patterns and requirements, not popularity. Default to a relational database like PostgreSQL for transactions, relationships and flexible queries. The shape of the data does not decide; how it is read and written does.

cards.title: How it works
cards.body: Key-value (DynamoDB, Redis) for simple lookups at scale, document stores for nested records, Cassandra for huge writes by known key, Elasticsearch for search, time-series for metrics. Blobs go to object storage. Multi-row ACID transactions force relational. Keep the truth in one store and sync others via CDC or an outbox.

questions.q: Why should Elasticsearch never be the source of truth?
questions.a: No transactions, near-real-time visibility, weaker durability, and it assumes the index can be rebuilt from the data it indexes.

questions.q: Why not write to every store in the request?
questions.a: Dual writes fail half-way with nothing to reconcile. Write to the source of truth and propagate via CDC or a transactional outbox.

questions.q: DynamoDB throttles while total capacity looks idle. Why?
questions.a: A hot partition: capacity is split across partitions and one key gets most traffic. Redesign the key or add write-sharding.
